Guidance for AI coding agents working with this repository.

Fizzy is a kanban-style project management and issue tracker: cards move across columns on boards, with comments, mentions, and assignments.

## Deploy

Default branch: `main`

Self-hosted deploys run Kamal against `config/deploy.yml` — see `docs/kamal-deployment.md`.

## SaaS mode

For local agent work, `tmp/saas.txt` is the checkout-level SaaS switch used by `bin/setup`. When present, read `saas/AGENTS.md` before continuing. Otherwise, do not apply its instructions.

## Architecture Overview

### Multi-Tenancy (URL-Based)

Fizzy uses **URL path-based multi-tenancy**:
- Accounts have a unique decimal `external_account_id` used in URL prefixes
- URLs are prefixed: `/{account_id}/boards/...`
- Middleware (`AccountSlug::Extractor`) extracts the account ID from the URL and sets `Current.account`
- The slug is moved from `PATH_INFO` to `SCRIPT_NAME`, making Rails think it's "mounted" at that path
- Tenant-scoped domain records are account-isolated; global identity, session, and authentication records are exceptions
- Background jobs automatically serialize and restore account context

**Key insight**: This architecture allows multi-tenancy without subdomains or separate databases, making local development and testing simpler.

### Authentication & Authorization

Passwordless magic link authentication. A global `Identity` (email-based) can have `Users` in multiple Accounts, so an email is not a single account membership. Users have roles: owner, admin, member, system. Board-level access control via `Access` records.

### Entropy System

Cards automatically "postpone" (move to "not now") after inactivity:
- Account-level default entropy period
- Board-level entropy override
- Prevents endless todo lists from accumulating
- Configurable via Account/Board settings

### UUID Primary Keys

All tables use UUIDs (UUIDv7 format, base36-encoded as 25-char strings):
- Custom fixture UUID generation maintains deterministic ordering for tests
- Fixtures are always "older" than runtime records
- `.first`/`.last` work correctly in tests

### Background Jobs (Solid Queue)

Database-backed job queue (no Redis):
- Custom `FizzyActiveJobExtensions` prepended to ActiveJob
- Jobs automatically capture/restore `Current.account`
- Mission Control::Jobs for monitoring

Recurring tasks are declared in `config/recurring.yml`.

### Sharded Full-Text Search

Full-text search runs in the database, not Elasticsearch. On MySQL it is sharded 16 ways by CRC32 of the account ID (`Search::Record::Trilogy`); on SQLite it is a single FTS5 index (`Search::Record::SQLite`). Don't assume the sharded shape when working under SQLite. Models in `app/models/search/`.

### Imports and exports

Allow people to move between OSS and SAAS Fizzy instances:
- Exports/Imports can be written to/read from local or S3 storage depending on the config of the instance (both must be supported)
- Must be able to handle very large ZIP files (500+GB)
- Models in `app/models/account/data_transfer/`, `app/models/zip_file`

## Coding style

Before editing or reviewing code, read STYLE.md.

class ZipFile
  class << self
    def create_for(attachment, filename:)
      raise ArgumentError, "No block given" unless block_given?

      reflection = attachment.record.class.reflect_on_attachment(attachment.name)
      service_name = reflection.options[:service_name] || ActiveStorage::Blob.service.name
      service = ActiveStorage::Blob.services.fetch(service_name)

      if s3_service?(service)
        create_for_s3(attachment, filename: filename, service: service) { |zip| yield zip }
      else
        create_for_disk(attachment, filename: filename) { |zip| yield zip }
      end
    end


    private
      def s3_service?(service)
        # The S3 service doesn't get loaded in development unless it's used
        defined?(ActiveStorage::Service::S3Service) && service.is_a?(ActiveStorage::Service::S3Service)
      end

      def create_for_s3(attachment, filename:, service:)
        blob = ActiveStorage::Blob.create_before_direct_upload!(
          filename: filename,
          content_type: "application/zip",
          byte_size: 0,
          checksum: "pending"
        )

        writer = Writer.new

        # Use S3's upload_stream directly for write-based streaming.
        # ActiveStorage's upload method expects a read-based IO, but ZipKit
        # needs a write-based stream. The TransferManager's upload_stream
        # yields a writable IO that we can stream directly to.
        service.send(:upload_stream,
          key: blob.key,
          content_type: "application/zip",
          part_size: 100.megabytes
        ) do |write_stream|
          write_stream.binmode
          writer.stream_to(write_stream)
          yield writer
          writer.close
        end

        blob.update!(byte_size: writer.byte_size, checksum: writer.checksum)
        attachment.attach(blob)
      rescue Aws::S3::MultipartUploadError => e
        if e.errors.any?
          raise e.errors.first
        else
          raise e
        end
      end

      def create_for_disk(attachment, filename:)
        tempfile = Tempfile.new([ "export", ".zip" ])
        tempfile.binmode

        writer = Writer.new(tempfile)
        yield writer
        writer.close

        tempfile.rewind
        attachment.attach(io: tempfile, filename: filename, content_type: "application/zip")
      ensure
        tempfile&.close
        tempfile&.unlink
      end

  end
end

# Style

We aim to write code that is a pleasure to read, and we have a lot of opinions about how to do it well. Writing great code is an essential part of our programming culture, and we deliberately set a high bar for every code change anyone contributes. We care about how code reads, how code looks, and how code makes you feel when you read it.

We love discussing code. If you have questions about how to write something, or if you detect some smell you are not quite sure how to solve, please ask away to other programmers. A Pull Request is a great way to do this.

When writing new code, unless you are very familiar with our approach, try to find similar code elsewhere to look for inspiration.

## Conditional returns

In general, we prefer to use expanded conditionals over guard clauses.

```ruby
# Bad
def todos_for_new_group
  ids = params.require(:todolist)[:todo_ids]
  return [] unless ids
  @bucket.recordings.todos.find(ids.split(","))
end

# Good
def todos_for_new_group
  if ids = params.require(:todolist)[:todo_ids]
    @bucket.recordings.todos.find(ids.split(","))
  else
    []
  end
end
```

This is because guard clauses can be hard to read, especially when they are nested.

As an exception, we sometimes use guard clauses to return early from a method:

* When the return is right at the beginning of the method.
* When the main method body is not trivial and involves several lines of code.

```ruby
def after_recorded_as_commit(recording)
  return if recording.parent.was_created?

  if recording.was_created?
    broadcast_new_column(recording)
  else
    broadcast_column_change(recording)
  end
end
```

## Methods ordering

We order methods in classes in the following order:

1. `class` methods
2. `public` methods with `initialize` at the top.
3. `private` methods

## Invocation order

We order methods vertically based on their invocation order. This helps us to understand the flow of the code.

```ruby
class SomeClass
  def some_method
    method_1
    method_2
  end

  private
    def method_1
      method_1_1
      method_1_2
    end
  
    def method_1_1
      # ...
    end
  
    def method_1_2
      # ...
    end
  
    def method_2
      method_2_1
      method_2_2
    end
  
    def method_2_1
      # ...
    end
  
    def method_2_2
      # ...
    end
end
```

## To bang or not to bang

Should I call a method `do_something` or `do_something!`?

As a general rule, we only use `!` for methods that have a correspondent counterpart without `!`. In particular, we don’t use `!` to flag destructive actions. There are plenty of destructive methods in Ruby and Rails that do not end with `!`.

## Visibility modifiers

We don't add a newline under visibility modifiers, and we indent the content under them.

```ruby
class SomeClass
  def some_method
    # ...
  end

  private
    def some_private_method_1
      # ...
    end

    def some_private_method_2
      # ...
    end
end
```

If a module only has private methods, we mark it `private` at the top and add an extra new line after but don't indent.

```ruby
module SomeModule
  private
  
  def some_private_method
    # ...
  end
end
```

## CRUD controllers

We model web endpoints as CRUD operations on resources (REST). When an action doesn't map cleanly to a standard CRUD verb, we introduce a new resource rather than adding custom actions.

```ruby
# Bad
resources :cards do
  post :close
  post :reopen
end

# Good
resources :cards do
  resource :closure
end
```

## Controller and model interactions

In general, we favor a [vanilla Rails](https://dev.37signals.com/vanilla-rails-is-plenty/) approach with thin controllers directly invoking a rich domain model. We don't use services or other artifacts to connect the two.

Invoking plain Active Record operations is totally fine:

```ruby
class Cards::CommentsController < ApplicationController
  def create
    @comment = @card.comments.create!(comment_params)
```

```ruby
class Cards::GoldnessesController < ApplicationController

end
```

When justified, it is fine to use services or form objects, but don't treat those as special artifacts:

```ruby
Signup.new(email_address: email_address).create_identity
```

## Run async operations in jobs

As a general rule, we write shallow job classes that delegate the logic itself to domain models:

* We typically use the suffix `_later` to flag methods that enqueue a job.
* A common scenario is having a model class that enqueues a job that, when executed, invokes some method in that same class. In this case, we use the suffix `_now` for the regular synchronous method.

```ruby
module Event::Relaying
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    after_create_commit :relay_later
  end

  def relay_later
    Event::RelayJob.perform_later(self)
  end

  def relay_now
    # ...
  end
end

class Event::RelayJob < ApplicationJob
  def perform(event)
    event.relay_now
  end
end
```

class ZipFile::Writer
  attr_reader :byte_size

  def initialize(io = nil)
    @entries = []
    @byte_size = 0
    @output_io = io
    @streamer = nil
    @digest = Digest::MD5.new
  end

  def stream_to(io)
    @output_io = io
  end

  def write(data)
    @output_io.write(data)
    @byte_size += data.bytesize
    @digest.update(data)
    data.bytesize
  end

  def add_file(path, content = nil, compress: true)
    @entries << path
    write_method = compress ? :write_deflated_file : :write_stored_file

    if block_given?
      streamer.public_send(write_method, path) { |sink| yield sink }
    else
      streamer.public_send(write_method, path) { |sink| sink.write(content) }
    end
  end

  def glob(pattern)
    @entries.select { |e| File.fnmatch(pattern, e) }.sort
  end

  def exists?(path)
    @entries.include?(path)
  end

  def close
    streamer.close
  end

  def checksum
    Base64.strict_encode64(@digest.digest)
  end

module Authentication
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    before_action :require_account # Checking and setting account must happen first
    before_action :require_authentication
    helper_method :authenticated?
    helper_method :email_address_pending_authentication

    etag { Current.identity.id if authenticated? }

    include Authentication::ViaMagicLink, LoginHelper
  end

  class_methods do
    def require_unauthenticated_access(**options)
      allow_unauthenticated_access **options
      before_action :redirect_authenticated_user, **options
    end

    def allow_unauthenticated_access(**options)
      skip_before_action :require_authentication, **options
      before_action :resume_session, **options
      allow_unauthorized_access **options
    end

    def disallow_account_scope(**options)
      skip_before_action :require_account, **options
      before_action :redirect_tenanted_request, **options
    end
  end

  private
    def authenticated?
      Current.identity.present?
    end

    def require_account
      unless Current.account.present?
        redirect_to main_app.session_menu_path(script_name: nil)
      end
    end

    def require_authentication
      resume_session || authenticate_by_bearer_token || request_authentication
    end

    def resume_session
      if session = find_session_by_cookie
        set_current_session session
      end
    end

    def find_session_by_cookie
      Session.find_signed(cookies.signed[:session_token])
    end

    def authenticate_by_bearer_token
      if request.authorization.to_s.include?("Bearer")
        if bearer_token_authenticatable_request?
          authenticate_or_request_with_http_token do |token|
            if identity = Identity.find_by_permissable_access_token(token, method: request.method)
              Current.identity = identity
            end
          end
        else
          request_http_token_authentication
        end
      end
    end

    def bearer_token_authenticatable_request?
      request.format.json?
    end

    def request_authentication
      if Current.account.present?
        session[:return_to_after_authenticating] = request.url
      end

      redirect_to_login_url
    end

    def after_authentication_url
      session.delete(:return_to_after_authenticating) || landing_url
    end

    def redirect_authenticated_user
      redirect_to main_app.root_url if authenticated?
    end

    def redirect_tenanted_request
      redirect_to main_app.root_url if Current.account.present?
    end

    def start_new_session_for(identity)
      identity.sessions.create!(user_agent: request.user_agent, ip_address: request.remote_ip).tap do |session|
        set_current_session session
      end
    end

    def set_current_session(session)
      Current.session = session
      cookies.signed.permanent[:session_token] = { value: session.signed_id, httponly: true, same_site: :lax }
    end

    def terminate_session
      Current.session.destroy
      cookies.delete(:session_token)
    end

    def session_token
      cookies[:session_token]

steps.reasoning_content:
Since the test file was emptied and upstream content removed, I'm trying to reconstruct the original RichTextRecordSet test cases from memory, recalling checks like rejecting rich text that references records from another account.

I'm also reconstructing the RichTextRecordSet class itself, recalling how it exports rich text records by converting embedded signed global IDs to plain global IDs for portability, and how import reverses that conversion back to sgids when loading batches of data.

I also recall the validation logic checking that each file's record ID matches its filename and that all required attributes are present, raising integrity errors otherwise, plus the helper that walks attachment nodes in the content to resolve and replace signed global IDs.

Then for the reverse direction, I'm writing the method that converts global IDs back to signed global IDs, filtering by account ownership, and then looking at the upstream record_set.rb class definition.

I'm tracing through the export/import logic: export writes records to a zip in batches, while import unpacks files and processes them in slices, skipping ahead if a start point is given.

Writing batch import and validation logic...

I'm also recalling how upstream handles identities during import—mapping exported user records by email address, using find_or_create_by to create Identity records, and checking how Account::Import determines ownership of the imported account.

On failure it marks the record failed and re-raises. I'm now recalling that upstream's import logic preserves original IDs from the export, which means re-importing into the same instance it came from would conflict with existing records—this seems designed for moving accounts between separate instances (OSS to SaaS), raising the question of whether same-instance re-import should even be supported.

To make it robust for same-instance imports, I think the better approach is remapping IDs: generate fresh UUIDs for every record and maintain an old-to-new mapping, which is more work but allows safe reuse on the same instance. The tricky part is that this mapping has to cover every foreign key, including polymorphic references like eventable_id, record_id, source_id, and notifiable, plus IDs buried inside JSON columns (tag_ids, board ids in filters) and rich text bodies referencing sgids or gids.

Keeping the original IDs and just failing on conflicts would be simpler, but it breaks the "bring the account back after it's gone" scenario unless the account was fully incinerated. I'm weighing the remapping approach against this simpler one, leaning toward remapping as the better product experience despite the added risk, and want to check how large the schema is before committing.

# Enforce storage ledger integrity by preventing blob reuse in tracked contexts.
#
# Two invariants:
# 1. Account match: blob.account_id == record.account_id (multi-tenant safety)
# 2. No reuse within tracked contexts: a blob can only have one tracked attachment
#
# With per-attachment reconcile, blob reuse inside an account wouldn't break correctness -
# ledger would still count each attach, and reconcile would agree. However, we intentionally
# forbid reuse (except templates) as a product/control decision:
# - Simpler mental model (one blob = one attachment)
# - Prevents accidental quota manipulation via direct blob_id reuse
# - Cleaner audit trail in ledger entries
#
# Scope note: The no-reuse validation only blocks reuse when the *new* attachment is tracked
# AND only checks *existing* attachments in Storage::TRACKED_RECORD_TYPES. A blob first
# attached to an untracked type (avatar/export) could theoretically be reused in a tracked
# context. This is acceptable - user-accessible blob IDs from untracked contexts are
# basically nonexistent in practice.
#
# Exception: ActionText embeds are allowed to reuse blobs to support copy/paste.

ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_storage_attachment) do
  validate :blob_account_matches_record, on: :create
  validate :no_tracked_blob_reuse, on: :create

  private
    # Multi-tenant safety: blob must belong to same account as record
    # NOTE: Skips validation if record.account is nil. This is a theoretical bypass
    # if someone attaches before account assignment, but our flows assign account
    # before attachment. Global/unaccounted attachments (Identity/User avatars, exports)
    # bypass tenancy checks via try(:account) returning nil - this is intentional as
    # these classes don't participate in storage tracking.
    def blob_account_matches_record
      if record&.try(:account).present? && !whitelisted_for_cross_account?
        unless blob&.account_id == record.account.id
          errors.add(:blob_id, "blob account must match record account")
        end
      end
    end

    # Ledger integrity: blob can only have one tracked attachment
    def no_tracked_blob_reuse
      tracked_record = record&.try(:storage_tracked_record)
      if tracked_record.present? &&
          !whitelisted_for_cross_account? &&
          !(record_type == "ActionText::RichText" && name == "embeds")

        # Check for existing attachment of this blob in tracked contexts
        # Uses Storage::TRACKED_RECORD_TYPES constant to stay generic
        existing = ActiveStorage::Attachment
          .where(blob_id: blob_id)
          .where(record_type: Storage::TRACKED_RECORD_TYPES)
          .where.not(id: id)
          .exists?

        if existing
          errors.add(:blob_id, "cannot reuse blob in tracked storage context")
        end
      end
    end

    def whitelisted_for_cross_account?
      # Only template account blobs can be reused cross-tenant.
      # When TEMPLATE_ACCOUNT_ID is nil, no exemptions are granted.
      Storage::TEMPLATE_ACCOUNT_ID.present? && blob&.account_id == Storage::TEMPLATE_ACCOUNT_ID
    end
end
# Fizzy-specific override: ActiveStorage's default purge path uses `delete`,
# which skips attachment callbacks. We need `destroy` so storage ledger detaches
# are recorded and reused blobs (ActionText embeds) aren't purged until the
# last attachment is gone. Keep this local to Fizzy; it's not a Rails default.
module ActiveStorage
  module PurgeOnLastAttachment
    def purge
      @purge_mode = :purge
      destroy
      purge_blob_if_last(:purge) if destroyed?
    ensure
      @purge_mode = nil
    end

    def purge_later
      @purge_mode = :purge_later
      destroy
      purge_blob_if_last(:purge_later) if destroyed?
    ensure
      @purge_mode = nil
    end

    private
      # Rails registers `after_destroy_commit :purge_dependent_blob` (renamed from
      # `purge_dependent_blob_later` upstream, which also now handles dependent: :purge).
      # Override the current callback name so reused blobs (ActionText embeds) are only
      # purged once the last attachment is gone, and skip when an explicit purge/purge_later
      # is already driving the blob purge via `purge_blob_if_last` (@purge_mode set).
      def purge_dependent_blob
        return if @purge_mode

        # `record.nil?` must be checked first: `dependent` reads `record.attachment_reflections`,
        # so it can't be evaluated for an orphaned attachment — an absent record falls back to
        # purge_later.
        if record.nil? || dependent == :purge_later
          purge_blob_if_last(:purge_later)
        elsif dependent == :purge
          purge_blob_if_last(:purge)
        end
      end

      def purge_blob_if_last(mode)
        if blob && !blob.attachments.exists?
          mode == :purge ? blob.purge : blob.purge_later
        end
      end
  end
end

ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_storage_attachment) do
  prepend ActiveStorage::PurgeOnLastAttachment
end

  "output": "# Serializes the current account into job data so that jobs run
# within the correct account context via Current.with_account.
#
# Account resolution is deferred to an around_perform callback so
# that missing accounts raise DeserializationError inside the
# execution path where discard_on can handle it.
module AccountTenanted
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  prepended do
    attr_reader :account
    around_perform :with_account_context
  end

  def initialize(...)
    super
    @account = Current.account
  end

  def serialize
    super.merge({ "account" => @account&.to_gid })
  end

  def deserialize(job_data)
    super
    @account_gid = job_data["account"]
  end

  private
    def with_account_context(&block)
      resolve_account!

      if account.present?
        Current.with_account(account, &block)
      else
        yield
      end
    end

    def resolve_account!
      if @account_gid
        @account = GlobalID::Locator.locate(@account_gid)
      end
    rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
      raise ActiveJob::DeserializationError
    end
end

steps.reasoning_content:
For file access I need the export's `accessible_to?(user)` check to restrict downloads to the user who created it, with the email linking to the export show page rather than the file directly so expiration can be enforced—exports expire after 24 hours and a recurring cleanup job destroys stale ones, with the show page scoping lookups to the current user's active exports.

Now I'm sketching account creation: the controller creates the account with a placeholder owner (named from the importer's email or existing identity name), attaching the import blob under the new account's context. The tricky part is that a half-imported account would otherwise appear in the session switcher before import finishes—I'm weighing whether to gate account visibility until import completes, or simply exclude in-progress accounts from the active accounts list shown in the session menu.

On the failure side, I need a clear `failure_reason` string to surface errors like invalid zip files, integrity conflicts, or a generic fallback message, and critically, a failed import should destroy the newly created account entirely (owner, boards, cards, everything cascading via dependent destroy) so nothing partial lingers.

I'm weighing whether a single giant transaction across the whole import is safe — it probably isn't, since it'd hold locks too long on SQLite or even MySQL. A more reliable cleanup approach is to explicitly delete every associated row by account_id across all imported models in reverse order using delete_all (skipping callbacks for speed), purge any uploaded blobs from storage, and then delete the account itself, guaranteeing nothing is left behind.

For blobs specifically, I'll delete each file from storage before removing its row. For identities created during import for new user emails, I need to track which ones were newly created and then, after destroying everything else, remove any of those identities that no longer have associated users. Since the import and cleanup happen in the same job/process, I can just keep the created identity ids in memory — though I recognize this cleanup won't run if the process is killed outright, which is an acceptable limitation for now.

On the actual zip reading approach, for files as large as 500GB I shouldn't download the whole thing to disk — I want to stream-read via random access. ZipKit's FileReader supports reading the central directory with random-access IO, and since ActiveStorage services expose `download_chunk(key, range)` for both disk and S3 backends, I can build a ranged IO adapter around that method and hand it to ZipKit for structure parsing.

class ZipKit::RemoteIO

  def initialize(url)

    @uri = URI(url)

  # Emulates IO#seek
  # @param offset[Integer] absolute offset in the remote resource to seek to
  # @param mode[Integer] The seek mode (only SEEK_SET is supported)

  # so if you are at offset 0 in the IO of size 10, doing a `read(20)`

  # @param n_bytes[Integer, nil] how many bytes to read, or `nil` to read all the way to the end
  # @return [String] the read bytes
  def read(n_bytes = nil)

    n_bytes ||= maximum_avaialable # nil == read to the end of file
    return "" if n_bytes.zero?
    raise ArgumentError, "No negative reads(#{n_bytes})" if n_bytes < 0

    n_bytes = clamp(0, n_bytes, maximum_avaialable)

    http_range = (@pos..(@pos + n_bytes - 1))
    request_range(http_range).tap do |data|
      raise "Remote read returned #{data.bytesize} bytes instead of #{n_bytes} as requested" if data.bytesize != n_bytes

I'm thinking I should subclass a remote IO class that downloads chunks from blob storage by key and range, using the blob's byte size for total length. Reading with local headers enabled would mean one range request per entry, which is too slow for large zips with many entries on S3, so I should disable that and lazily read local headers per entry during extraction instead.

I can compute the compressed data offset on demand when it's not yet known, raising a pending error otherwise. For the local disk service, opening the file per chunk download is cheap enough to not worry about. For extraction, I'll read through an inflating reader in moderate-sized chunks, and for uploading extracted blobs back to ActiveStorage, I'll write to a tempfile first since that handles large files fine without needing to stream directly into the upload API.

Now I'm distinguishing the two export types: the user-facing export bundles per-card JSON (including comments) plus attached files and pictures, while the account-level export dumps the full data model as data/<table>/<id>.json alongside storage/<key> blobs. I'm sketching out how User::DataExport would iterate over the user's accessible cards, adding each card's JSON and its attachments into the zip under a folder named after the card number.

I'm also weighing whether the account export should additionally include a human-readable `cards/` folder with card JSON like the user export does, but that risks duplicating a lot of file content, so I need to decide how much overlap is worth the extra readability.

Defining per-card JSON attachment structure with filename, content type, byte size, and a path pointing into the zip, differing slightly between user and account export formats. I'm also planning a manifest file with version and export metadata so imports can validate the file is a genuine Fizzy export, then sketching the database migrations needed: an `exports` table with account/user references and status tracking, and an `account_imports` table with similar fields.

Now I'm thinking through the model layer: a base `Export` class with attachment handling, status enum, and helper methods for downloadability and access control, with subclasses for account exports and user data exports. I'm also outlining supporting classes like `Account::Import`, a zip reader utility, record set export/import logic, mailers for completion/failure notifications, and background jobs to handle the actual export/import work asynchronously.

For naming, I'm settling on `DataExportJob` and `ImportAccountDataJob` to match likely upstream conventions, plus a recurring cleanup task for stale exports and imports. I'm also mapping out the controllers (account exports, user data exports, account imports with appropriate authorization scoping), their corresponding views and mail templates, and the routes needed to tie it all together, along with storage tracking via an included module.

Since bulk attachment inserts bypass normal callbacks, I need to reconcile storage totals after import completes, which points me toward `Account::Storage` and a `Storage::ReconcileJob` to handle that recalculation.

  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

    # Snapshot IDs in before_destroy since parent record may be deleted

    before_destroy :snapshot_storage_context
    after_create_commit :record_storage_attach
    after_destroy_commit :record_storage_detach

      return unless storage_tracked_record

      Storage::Entry.record \
        account: storage_tracked_record.account,
        board: storage_tracked_record.board_for_storage_tracking,

        delta: blob.byte_size,

      return unless @storage_snapshot

      Storage::Entry.record \
        account: @storage_snapshot[:account],
        board: @storage_snapshot[:board],
        recordable: @storage_snapshot[:recordable],
        blob: blob,
        delta: -blob.byte_size,

        board: storage_tracked_record.board_for_storage_tracking,

  "output": "# Repair task — reindexes every searchable Card and Comment in the database.
# Intended to be invoked manually after a search-index loss event. Not a recurring job.
#
# Idempotent: Searchable#reindex upserts by (searchable_type, searchable_id).
# Continuable: if the worker is interrupted, the job resumes from the last-processed id.
#
# `rich_text_limit` is a safety valve against unbounded bodies: records whose rich text
# exceeds the limit (in bytes) are filtered out at the SQL level, so they never materialize
# in Ruby. Without it, a single pathological body can stall the batch query or OOM the
# worker during preload, which has happened in practice.
#
# Usage:
#   SearchReindexJob.perform_later
#   SearchReindexJob.perform_later(batch_size: 500, log_every: 100, rich_text_limit: 50_000)
class SearchReindexJob < ApplicationJob
  include ActiveJob::Continuable

  queue_as :backend

  def perform(batch_size: 100, log_every: 1000, rich_text_limit: 100_000)
    step :cards do |step|
      processed = 0
      Card.published
          .left_joins(:rich_text_description)
          .where("action_text_rich_texts.body IS NULL OR OCTET_LENGTH(action_text_rich_texts.body) <= ?", rich_text_limit)
          .includes(:rich_text_description)
          .find_each(start: step.cursor, batch_size: batch_size) do |card|
        safely_reindex(card)
        processed += 1
        log_progress(:cards, processed, card.id) if (processed % log_every).zero?
        step.advance! from: card.id
      end
    end

    step :comments do |step|
      processed = 0
      Comment.joins(:card).merge(Card.published)
             .left_joins(:rich_text_body)
             .where("action_text_rich_texts.body IS NULL OR OCTET_LENGTH(action_text_rich_texts.body) <= ?", rich_text_limit)
             .includes(:rich_text_body, :card)
             .find_each(start: step.cursor, batch_size: batch_size) do |comment|
        safely_reindex(comment)
        processed += 1
        log_progress(:comments, processed, comment.id) if (processed % log_every).zero?
        step.advance! from: comment.id
      end
    end
  end

  private
    def safely_reindex(record)
      record.reindex
    rescue StandardError => e
      Rails.error.report(e, context: { record_type: record.class.name, record_id: record.id })
    end

    def log_progress(step_name, count, cursor)
      Rails.logger.info { "SearchReindexJob: step=#{step_name} processed=#{count} cursor=#{cursor}" }
    end
end

steps.reasoning_content:
Rich text attachments embed signed global IDs (sgid) that are tied to the app's secret_key_base, so they won't verify across instances—I need to convert sgid to gid on export and back to sgid on import, matching how the upstream RichTextRecordSet handles this, since the underlying IDs themselves stay stable.

Mention attachments for users work the same way. I'm also considering the url attribute embedded in attachments, which includes the account slug and a signed blob ID, but since rendering regenerates blob URLs fresh via the blob partial, that's less of a concern. For detecting attachments in the body, I can parse the HTML for action-text-attachment elements with sgid attributes and use SignedGlobalID.parse with the "attachable" locator name rather than doing a full database lookup.

The key security concern is that an imported gid could reference a record from another account entirely -- someone could craft a file pointing to another account's blob and gain a valid sgid to view that data, which would be a leak. So on import, for each gid I need to locate the actual record and verify its account_id matches the importing account before converting it to an sgid, dropping the node otherwise. Since rich texts are imported after blobs and users, this lookup should work fine, and doing it per-record rather than batched is acceptable for performance. I also need to handle other attachable types like RemoteImage that don't use sgid at all, just a plain URL.

Rich text embeds (attachment blobs) get imported through the AttachmentRecordSet, which is already handled. Other sensitive data like webhook signing_secret, board publication keys, and params_digest should carry over fine since they're preserved values. For users, I need to map the exported identity email to an Identity record via find_or_create, with system-role users having no identity. I should also double check that ActiveStorage blob keys, which have a unique index, won't collide on import.

I'm planning a shared `Card::Exportable#export_data` method reused by both export types, with the account export referencing storage blobs by key, and the import process simply skipping the `cards/` directory since it's just for readability.

For the per-user export, I'm deciding which cards to include—published cards visible to the user plus their own drafts—and working out file paths for attachments, nesting files under `cards/<number>/` with uniquified filenames to avoid collisions. I'm drafting the card JSON shape with fields like number, title, status, board, and column.

I also need to decide how to represent comments and rich text bodies, since `action-text-attachment` tags embed attachments inline and rendering `to_html` normally needs a view context—I'll need to figure out how to render that server-side for the export, alongside plain-text and HTML versions of each body.

For downloading, I need the show page to link to the file via rails_blob_path with attachment disposition, relying on Export#accessible_to? to check that the current user owns the export. The signed blob id doesn't expire by default, but the redirect route generates a short-lived service URL, so the email link to the export page still enforces the 24-hour check and expired exports get cleaned up along with their files.

I should also make Export#accessible_to? return false once expired, since otherwise the blob redirect route could still work past 24h before cleanup runs. I'll add a rate limit, something like 10 exports per day, returning a 429 if exceeded.

Now I'm shifting to the Account::Import flow — setting up an untenanted controller for new/create actions that starts an import tied to the current identity and uploaded file, and thinking through direct upload support since files could be as large as 500GB.

The trouble is direct uploads need the blob tied to an account, but the import creation page is untenanted, so there's no Current.account yet, which would make the blob insert fail on a NOT NULL constraint. This pushes me toward a two-step flow: first create the account and a pending import record untenanted, redirect into the account-scoped import page, and only then handle the direct upload and kick off the import — more complex UX, but it handles huge files reliably.

Actually, I think a simpler route works better: have the controller create the account first, then run the import creation (with the file attached) inside Current.with_account so the blob gets the right account_id, using a regular multipart upload rather than direct upload. This won't scale to truly massive files behind proxies, but I could offer a rake task or CLI import path for those as a future nice-to-have, and focus the job itself on validating the zip contents before processing them.

After processing, I finalize by reindexing and reconciling storage, mark as completed, and send a completion email — wrapping everything in a rescue that marks the job failed, records a failure reason, and tears down the created account/data so nothing orphaned remains. I'm deciding not to re-raise expected validation errors since the account cleanup already handles that case, but I do want unexpected errors reported to Rails.error for visibility without retrying (since there's no account left to retry against). I'm also mapping out exactly what gets destroyed when the account is torn down — users and their dependent comments, filters, pins, and other associated records — to make sure the cleanup is thorough.

Instead of relying on cascading destroys through callbacks (which could be slow or error-prone if the imported data is inconsistent), I'm considering a more deterministic approach: introspecting all tables with an account_id column and deleting rows directly by account_id, plus handling join tables, search records, storage entries, and blob files through their appropriate service calls, before finally removing the account row itself. This feels more thorough and predictable for leaving nothing behind.

Actually, partial imports could leave dangling references—comments without rich texts, events with missing eventables—so destroy callbacks might break halfway through. I think a hard delete is more robust here. For storage, I'd iterate over the account's blobs and delete both the underlying files and the rows directly, and I need to remember that variant records also carry their own attached blobs that need cleanup too.

Now I'm thinking through how `Storage::Entry` records get reconciled after import, since bulk-inserting attachments skips normal tracking—so I'll need to call the account's reconcile and recalculate real storage bytes per board, then materialize storage afterward. I'm also working out user-friendly validation error messages for each phase: checking the manifest is present and versioned correctly, and for each record set verifying valid JSON, matching ids, required attributes, and guarding against importing into an account that already has this data.

There's a deeper security concern I'm working through: a maliciously crafted export could reference records belonging to other accounts—like a Comment whose card_id points to a foreign account's card while its account_id gets overwritten to the importing account. Since comments are rendered through their card association rather than strict account scoping, this could leak or inject data into another account's card, which I need to guard against with proper foreign-key validation during import.

A cleaner approach is post-import verification using SQL queries per association: check that each belongs_to foreign key either points to nil or to a record within the same target account, running this after all data is inserted but before finalizing, and rolling back everything on any violation. For polymorphic associations I'd verify each distinct type similarly, failing on unrecognized types. I can derive the associations to check from each model's belongs_to reflections (excluding account itself) — Card references board/creator/column, Comment references card/creator, Event references creator/board, and so on.

Rather than hardcoding every model's associations, I'm leaning toward introspecting them dynamically via the model's belongs_to reflections, skipping account and identity since those are handled separately.

For resolving the target class of each reflection, I check whether its table has an account_id column, skipping ones like Identity that don't. For polymorphic associations I'd need to pluck distinct types and constantize safely against an allowlist of manifest model names plus "Account" itself.

I'm also realizing a subtler risk: an attacker could include user records whose emails match other real users, which would mean imported users get assigned the identity_id of an existing victim rather than a new one — effectively linking the imported account to someone else's identity and making it appear in their account list.

That's not a data leak per se, more like an uninvited grant of account membership, which is actually necessary for the legitimate "invite people" use case, so I'll treat it as acceptable. Imported users shouldn't get live sessions or access tokens though, and their verified_at status should just carry over as-is.

I'm skipping resumability features to keep the design simple, and I'm sketching a reader API mirroring the writer — glob, exists?, and read methods that can stream chunks — plus thinking about indexing entries by directory to avoid repeatedly globbing over potentially a million filenames per record type.

For performance I'm grouping entries by dirname so I only fnmatch against the relevant subset rather than the whole million-entry list, keeping pattern matching fast.   def extract(n_bytes = nil)
    n_bytes ||= (@compressed_data_size - @already_read)

    return if eof?

    available = @compressed_data_size - @already_read

    return if available.zero?

To avoid N+1 queries during existence checks, I'm planning to batch the id lookups using a single where/pluck query. I'm also weighing the risk that strict attribute requirements could break imports from older export versions that are missing newly added columns.

Refining required attributes to just the id plus any NOT NULL columns without defaults, excluding account_id since that's set separately—computing this dynamically from the model's column metadata so it adapts automatically as the schema evolves. For importing, I'm working out how to handle rows with varying keys since insert_all needs consistent columns across all rows, so I need to normalize each row by filling in missing attributes with their column defaults.

For timestamps, insert_all in Rails 7+ handles created_at/updated_at automatically when they're not explicitly provided, which simplifies things. I'm also thinking through how different model types (ActiveStorage::Blob, ActionText::RichText, etc.) get their table names and how exporting a record's JSON representation should work by slicing its attributes.

Now I'm working through post-import integrity checks: verifying belongs_to references for each model, handling polymorphic associations by distinguishing allowed classes, special-casing Account references, and counting any foreign keys that don't resolve to valid scoped records.

Some reflections use `class_name` that might raise on klass resolution, so I'll rescue NameError and skip those. For Filter habtm join tables, I need to verify join ids exist within the account inside FilterRecordSet, and for record sets generally I'm scoping by `account_id: account.id`, with placeholder owner users still belonging correctly to the account even if not imported.

For card number uniqueness, since imported cards keep their original numbers scoped to (account_id, number), I need to make sure the account's cards_count is set to at least the maximum imported card number after import finishes.

Now I'm working out AccountRecordSet specifics: exporting all columns to a JSON file, skipping the "already exists" check since conflicts elsewhere would already be caught, and having import simply update the account's name and cards_count. For UserRecordSet, I'm exporting all columns plus a derived email_address from the identity, and in import_batch handling identity lookup/creation per user along with placeholder account cases.

For the system-role placeholder, I'm figuring out that I need to capture the account's existing users before import starts so I can identify which ones are placeholders, then destroy the placeholder system user or owner once the real imported user with a matching identity takes its place—being mindful that destroying a user triggers its dependent associations (comments, etc.) and that the account's system_user reference needs to stay consistent.

I also need to check email format validity for users during this phase, and handle EntropyRecordSet import correctly: rows with container_type "Account" update the account's entropy auto_postpone_period directly rather than being inserted, while rewriting container_id references to the current account works fine since those rows skip insertion anyway. For BlobRecordSet, I'm verifying that blobs get inserted with the correct service_name, confirming the storage file exists in the zip with matching byte_size, and checking blob key uniqueness.

Key validation is critical here since keys map directly to storage file paths — a malicious key with path traversal sequences could escape the storage root on the disk service. I need to validate that keys match the expected format (alphanumeric for standard blobs, and the slash-separated variant pattern for variant keys like "variants/<blobkey>/<digest>") to prevent any path traversal attack.

For the export logic, I'm considering what happens when a blob references a file that's actually missing from storage — I'm leaning toward skipping missing files during export with a warning rather than failing the entire export, since one missing file shouldn't block an otherwise valid backup.

On import, I'll mirror that tolerance: if a blob's file isn't in the zip, just leave the attachment unuploaded rather than erroring, since that matches the broken state in the source. When the file is present, I'll extract it to a tempfile respecting the byte_size limit and upload it through the storage service with checksum verification, letting integrity mismatches raise naturally. I also need to track which keys get uploaded so cleanup can properly remove them later if needed.

For RichTextRecordSet, I'm handling body conversions between sgid and gid references using Nokogiri to parse the raw HTML before type casting, then reconstructing the content. On export, invalid or unparsable sgid nodes should probably be left untouched rather than stripped, since import will naturally fail to resolve them into renderable attachments if they're foreign. class Account::DataTransfer::RecordSet
  class IntegrityError < StandardError; end

  INTERNAL_RECORD_TYPES = %w[Export].freeze
  BATCH_SIZE = 100
  MAX_RECORD_SIZE = 100.megabytes

  attr_reader :account, :model, :attributes

  def initialize(account:, model:, attributes: nil)
    @account = account
    @model = model
    @attributes = (attributes || model.column_names).map(&:to_s)
  end

  def export(to:)
    with_zip(to) do
      each_record { |record| export_record(record) }
    end
  end

  # Validates the records in the archive without writing anything.
  def check(from:)
    with_zip(from) do
      files.each_slice(BATCH_SIZE) do |batch|
        check_batch(batch.map { |file| [ file, load(file) ] })
      end
    end
  end

  def import(from:)
    with_zip(from) do
      files.each_slice(BATCH_SIZE) do |batch|
        import_batch(batch.map { |file| load(file) })
      end
    end
  end

  # Runs after everything is imported: every reference must point at a record in the
  # imported account, so a crafted file can't reach into other accounts.
  def verify_references
    belongs_to_reflections.each do |reflection|
      if reflection.polymorphic?
        verify_polymorphic_reference(reflection)
      else
        verify_reference(reflection.foreign_key, reflection.klass)
      end
    end
  end

  def to_s
    model_dir.humanize(capitalize: false)
  end

  private
    attr_reader :zip

    def with_zip(zip)
      old_zip = @zip
      @zip = zip
      yield
    ensure
      @zip = old_zip
    end

    def records
      model.where(account_id: account.id)
    end

    def model_dir
      model.table_name
    end

    def each_record(&block)
      if records.respond_to?(:find_each)
        records.find_each(&block)
      else
        records.each(&block)
      end
    end

    def export_record(record)
      zip.add_file path_for(record.id), serialize(record).to_json
    end

    def path_for(id)
      "data/#{model_dir}/#{id}.json"
    end

    def serialize(record)
      record.attributes.slice(*attributes).transform_values { |value| serialize_value(value) }
    end

    def serialize_value(value)
      case value
      when ActiveSupport::TimeWithZone, Time, DateTime then value.utc.iso8601(6)
      else value
      end
    end

    def files
      zip.glob("data/#{model_dir}/*.json")
    end

    def load(file)
      JSON.parse(zip.read(file, limit: MAX_RECORD_SIZE)).tap do |data|
        raise IntegrityError, "#{file} doesn't contain a record" unless data.is_a?(Hash)
      end
    rescue JSON::ParserError
      raise IntegrityError, "#{file} isn't valid JSON"
    rescue ZipFile::Reader::InvalidFileError => error
      raise IntegrityError, error.message
    end

    def check_batch(batch)
      batch.each { |file, data| check_record(file, data) }
      check_conflicts(batch.map { |_, data| data["id"] })
    end

    def check_record(file, data)
      unless data["id"].to_s == File.basename(file, ".json")
        raise IntegrityError, "#{file} has a mismatched ID (#{data["id"].inspect})"
      end

      if (missing = required_attributes - data.keys).any?
        raise IntegrityError, "#{file} is missing required fields: #{missing.to_sentence}"
      end
    end

    def required_attributes
      @required_attributes ||= model.columns
        .select { |column| !column.null && column.default.nil? && column.name.in?(attributes) }
        .map(&:name) - %w[ account_id ]
    end

    def check_conflicts(ids)
      if (existing = model.where(id: ids).pick(:id))
        raise IntegrityError, "The #{model.model_name.human.downcase} #{existing} already exists in this Fizzy. " \
          "If you are bringing back an account that is still here, delete it first."
      end
    end

    def import_batch(batch)
      model.insert_all!(batch.map { |data| row_for(data) })
    end

    def row_for(data)
      attributes.index_with { |attribute| data.fetch(attribute) { model.column_defaults[attribute] } }
        .merge("account_id" => account.id)
    end

    def belongs_to_reflections
      model.reflect_on_all_associations(:belongs_to).reject do |reflection|
        reflection.name.in?(%i[ account identity ]) || !model.column_names.include?(reflection.foreign_key.to_s) ||
          (!reflection.polymorphic? && !tenanted?(reflection.klass))
      end
    end

    def tenanted?(klass)
      klass.column_names.include?("account_id")
    end

    def verify_polymorphic_reference(reflection)
      records.where.not(reflection.foreign_type => nil).distinct.pluck(reflection.foreign_type).each do |type|
        klass = Account::DataTransfer::Manifest.model_named(type)
        scope = records.where(reflection.foreign_type => type)

        if klass.nil?
          raise IntegrityError, "Some #{self} point to an unsupported kind of record (#{type})"
        elsif klass == Account
          if scope.where.not(reflection.foreign_key => account.id).exists?
            raise IntegrityError, "Some #{self} belong to a different account"
          end
        else
          verify_reference(reflection.foreign_key, klass, scope: scope)
        end
      end
    end

    def verify_reference(foreign_key, klass, scope: records)
      orphaned = scope.where.not(foreign_key => nil)
        .where.not(foreign_key => klass.unscoped.where(account_id: account.id).select(:id))

      if (orphan = orphaned.pick(:id))
        raise IntegrityError, "The #{model.model_name.human.downcase} #{orphan} points to a #{klass.model_name.human.downcase} that isn't in this file"
      end
    end
end
EOF

class Account::DataTransfer::UserRecordSet < Account::DataTransfer::RecordSet
  attr_reader :created_identity_ids

  def initialize(account)
    super(account: account, model: User, attributes: User.column_names - %w[ identity_id ])
    @created_identity_ids = []
  end

  def import(from:)
    @placeholders = account.users.includes(:identity).to_a
    super
  end

  private
    def records
      User.where(account: account).includes(:identity)
    end

    def serialize(user)
      super.merge("email_address" => user.identity&.email_address)
    end

    def check_record(file, data)
      super

      if data["email_address"].present? && !data["email_address"].to_s.match?(URI::MailTo::EMAIL_REGEXP)
        raise IntegrityError, "#{file} has an invalid email address"
      end

      unless data["role"].in?(User.roles.keys)
        raise IntegrityError, "#{file} has an unknown role (#{data["role"].inspect})"
      end
    end

    def import_batch(batch)
      rows = batch.map do |data|
        identity = identity_for(data["email_address"])
        replace_placeholder_for(data, identity)
        row_for(data).merge("identity_id" => identity&.id)
      end

      User.insert_all!(rows)
    end

    def identity_for(email_address)
      if email_address.present?
        Identity.find_or_create_by!(email_address: email_address).tap do |identity|
          created_identity_ids << identity.id if identity.previously_new_record?
        end
      end
    end

    # The account comes with a system user and an owner for whoever is importing. When the
    # file has its own versions of them, those win so every reference in the file resolves.
    def replace_placeholder_for(data, identity)
      placeholder = @placeholders.find do |user|
        (data["role"] == "system" && user.system?) || (identity && user.identity_id == identity.id)
      end

      if placeholder
        @placeholders.delete(placeholder)
        placeholder.destroy!
      end
    end
end
EOF

# Moves the stored files themselves, under storage/<blob key>. Runs after the blob records exist.
class Account::DataTransfer::ActiveStorage::FileRecordSet < Account::DataTransfer::RecordSet
  def initialize(account)
    super(account: account, model: ::ActiveStorage::Blob)
  end

  def verify_references
  end

  private
    def records
      ::ActiveStorage::Blob.where(account: account).where.not(id: excluded_blob_ids)
    end

    def excluded_blob_ids
      ::ActiveStorage::Attachment.where(account: account, record_type: INTERNAL_RECORD_TYPES).select(:blob_id)
    end

    def export_record(blob)
      zip.add_file file_path_for(blob.key), compress: false do |sink|
        blob.download { |chunk| sink.write(chunk) }
      end
    rescue ::ActiveStorage::FileNotFoundError
      Rails.logger.warn "[DataTransfer] Skipping missing file for blob #{blob.id}"
    end

    def file_path_for(key)
      "storage/#{key}"
    end

    # Blob records are validated by BlobRecordSet; here we only make sure files match their records.
    def check_batch(batch)
      batch.each do |file, data|
        path = file_path_for(data["key"])

        if zip.exists?(path) && zip.size_of(path) != data["byte_size"].to_i
          raise IntegrityError, "#{path} doesn't match the size of the original file"
        end
      end
    end

    def import_batch(batch)
      ::ActiveStorage::Blob.where(account: account, id: batch.map { |data| data["id"] }).each do |blob|
        upload(blob) if zip.exists?(file_path_for(blob.key))
      end
    end

    def upload(blob)
      Tempfile.create([ "import", File.extname(blob.filename.to_s) ], binmode: true) do |tempfile|
        zip.read(file_path_for(blob.key), limit: blob.byte_size) { |chunk| tempfile.write(chunk) }
        tempfile.rewind

        blob.service.upload(blob.key, tempfile, checksum: blob.checksum.presence)
      end
    rescue ::ActiveStorage::IntegrityError
      raise IntegrityError, "The file #{blob.filename} is corrupted"
    rescue ZipFile::Reader::InvalidFileError => error
      raise IntegrityError, error.message
    end
end
EOF

# Signed global IDs in rich text bodies only verify on the instance that signed them, so
# exports carry plain global IDs instead, which are signed again on import. Attachments
# pointing at records outside the account are dropped.
class Account::DataTransfer::ActionText::RichTextRecordSet < Account::DataTransfer::RecordSet
  ATTACHMENT_SELECTOR = ::ActionText::Attachment.tag_name

  def initialize(account)
    super(account: account, model: ::ActionText::RichText)
  end

  private
    def records
      ::ActionText::RichText.where(account: account)
    end

    def serialize(rich_text)
      super.merge("body" => convert_sgids_to_gids(rich_text.read_attribute_before_type_cast(:body)))
    end

    def row_for(data)
      super.merge("body" => convert_gids_to_sgids(data["body"]))
    end

    def convert_sgids_to_gids(html)
      transform_attachments(html) do |node|
        if node["sgid"] && (sgid = SignedGlobalID.parse(node["sgid"], for: ::ActionText::Attachable::LOCATOR_NAME))
          node["gid"] = sgid.to_s.sub(/\A[^?]*\z/) { GlobalID.new(sgid.uri).to_s }
          node.remove_attribute("sgid")
        end
      end
    end

    def convert_gids_to_sgids(html)
      transform_attachments(html) do |node|
        record = attachable_for(node)
        node.remove_attribute("gid")

        if record
          node["sgid"] = record.attachable_sgid
        else
          node.remove_attribute("sgid")
        end
      end
    end

    def transform_attachments(html)
      if html.blank? || !html.include?(ATTACHMENT_SELECTOR)
        html
      else
        fragment = Nokogiri::HTML5.fragment(html)
        fragment.css(ATTACHMENT_SELECTOR).each { |node| yield node }
        fragment.to_html
      end
    end

    def attachable_for(node)
      global_id = if node["gid"]
        GlobalID.parse(node["gid"])
      elsif node["sgid"]
        SignedGlobalID.parse(node["sgid"], for: ::ActionText::Attachable::LOCATOR_NAME)
      end

      if global_id && (model = Account::DataTransfer::Manifest.model_named(global_id.model_name))
        model.find_by(id: global_id.model_id, account_id: account.id) if tenanted?(model)
      end
    end
end
EOF

# Saved filters keep their boards, tags and people in join tables, so those ids travel
# inside each filter's JSON.
class Account::DataTransfer::FilterRecordSet < Account::DataTransfer::RecordSet
  def initialize(account)
    super(account: account, model: Filter)
  end

  def verify_references
    super

    join_associations.each do |association|
      join_model = join_model_for(association)
      foreign_key = association.association_foreign_key

      orphaned = join_model.where(filter_id: records.select(:id))
        .where.not(foreign_key => association.klass.where(account_id: account.id).select(:id))

      if orphaned.exists?
        raise IntegrityError, "Some saved filters point to #{association.name} that aren't in this file"
      end
    end
  end

  private
    def records
      super.includes(join_associations.map(&:name))
    end

    def serialize(filter)
      super.merge(join_associations.to_h { |association| [ ids_key_for(association), filter.public_send(association.name).ids ] })
    end

    def import_batch(batch)
      super

      join_associations.each do |association|
        rows = batch.flat_map do |data|
          Array(data[ids_key_for(association)]).map { |id| { "filter_id" => data["id"], association.association_foreign_key => id } }
        end

        join_model_for(association).insert_all!(rows) if rows.any?
      end
    end

    def join_associations
      Filter.reflect_on_all_associations(:has_and_belongs_to_many)
    end

    def join_model_for(association)
      Filter.reflect_on_association(association.join_table).klass
    end

    def ids_key_for(association)
      "#{association.name.to_s.singularize}_ids"
    end
end
EOF

    processing!

# Every card the person can see, as JSON with its comments, plus the files attached to it.
class User::DataExport < Export
  private
    def populate_zip(zip)
      exportable_cards.find_each do |card|
        add_card_to(zip, card)
      end
    end

    def exportable_cards
      user.accessible_cards
        .where(status: :published).or(user.accessible_cards.where(creator: user))
        .includes(:board, :column, :creator, :tags, :assignees, :steps)
    end

    def add_card_to(zip, card)
      paths = file_paths_for(card)

      zip.add_file "cards/#{card.number}.json", JSON.pretty_generate(card.export_data(file_path: ->(blob) { paths[blob] }).as_json)

      paths.each do |blob, path|
        add_file_to(zip, blob, path)
      end
    end

    def file_paths_for(card)
      taken = Set.new

      card.exportable_blobs.index_with do |blob|
        unique_path("cards/#{card.number}/#{blob.filename.sanitized}", taken).tap { |path| taken << path }
      end
    end

    def unique_path(path, taken)
      extension = File.extname(path)
      base = path.delete_suffix(extension)

      candidates = Enumerator.produce(1) { it + 1 }.lazy.map { |n| n == 1 ? path : "#{base} (#{n})#{extension}" }
      candidates.find { |candidate| !taken.include?(candidate) }
    end

    def add_file_to(zip, blob, path)
      zip.add_file path, compress: false do |sink|
        blob.download { |chunk| sink.write(chunk) }
      end
    rescue ActiveStorage::FileNotFoundError
      Rails.logger.warn "[DataExport] Skipping missing file for blob #{blob.id}"
    end

    def filename_subject
      "#{account.name} #{user.name}"
    end
end
EOF

# Brings an account export (see Account::Export) back in as a brand new account.
#
# The account is created up front so the uploaded file lives in it. Everything in the file is
# validated before anything is written, and if the import fails at any point, the account and
# everything imported into it are removed.
class Account::Import < ApplicationRecord
  class InvalidFileError < StandardError; end

  PLACEHOLDER_ACCOUNT_NAME = "Importing…"
  GENERIC_FAILURE_REASON = "Something went wrong on our end while importing the file."

  belongs_to :account, optional: true
  belongs_to :identity

  has_one_attached :file

  enum :status, %w[ pending processing completed failed ].index_by(&:itself), default: :pending

  validate :file_must_be_a_zip, on: :create

  class << self
    def start(identity:, file:)
      account = create_account_for(identity)

      Current.with_account(account) do
        create!(account: account, identity: identity, file: file).tap(&:process_later)
      end
    rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid
      account&.destroy
      raise
    end

    private
      def create_account_for(identity)
        Account.create_with_owner \
          account: { name: PLACEHOLDER_ACCOUNT_NAME },
          owner: { name: name_for(identity), identity: identity }
      end

      def name_for(identity)
        identity.users.where.not(name: [ nil, "" ]).order(:created_at).last&.name || identity.email_address.split("@").first
      end
  end

  def process_later
    ImportAccountDataJob.perform_later(self)
  end

  def process
    processing!

    import_file
    finish

    update!(status: :completed, completed_at: Time.current)
    file.purge_later
    ImportMailer.completed(self).deliver_later
  rescue => error
    fail_with error
  end

  private
    def file_must_be_a_zip
      if !file.attached?
        errors.add(:file, "must be attached")
      elsif !file.filename.extension.to_s.casecmp?("zip")
        errors.add(:file, "must be a .zip file exported from Fizzy")
      end
    end

    def import_file
      ZipFile.read_from(file.blob) do |zip|
        check_manifest(zip)

        record_sets.each { |record_set| record_set.check(from: zip) }
        record_sets.each { |record_set| record_set.import(from: zip) }
        record_sets.each(&:verify_references)
      end
    rescue ZipFile::Reader::InvalidFileError => error
      raise InvalidFileError, "The file isn't a valid ZIP archive. Make sure you upload the .zip file exactly as you downloaded it from Fizzy."
    end

    def record_sets
      @record_sets ||= [].tap do |record_sets|
        Account::DataTransfer::Manifest.new(account).each_record_set { |record_set| record_sets << record_set }
      end
    end

    def check_manifest(zip)
      manifest = JSON.parse(zip.read(Account::DataTransfer::Manifest::PATH, limit: 1.megabyte)) if zip.exists?(Account::DataTransfer::Manifest::PATH)

      unless manifest.is_a?(Hash) && manifest["format"] == Account::DataTransfer::Manifest::FORMAT
        raise InvalidFileError, "The file isn't a Fizzy account export. You can download one from an account's settings."
      end

      if manifest["version"].to_i > Account::DataTransfer::Manifest::VERSION
        raise InvalidFileError, "The file was exported from a newer version of Fizzy. Update this Fizzy and try again."
      end
    rescue JSON::ParserError
      raise InvalidFileError, "The file isn't a Fizzy account export. You can download one from an account's settings."
    end

    def finish
      account.update!(cards_count: [ account.cards_count, account.cards.maximum(:number).to_i ].max)

      ensure_importer_can_access_account
      reindex_search
      reconcile_storage
    end

    def ensure_importer_can_access_account
      user = account.users.find_or_initialize_by(identity: identity)
      user.update!(name: user.name.presence || self.class.send(:name_for, identity), role: :owner, active: true, verified_at: user.verified_at || Time.current) unless user.persisted? && user.active?

      account.boards.all_access.find_each { |board| board.accesses.grant_to(user) }
    end

    def reindex_search
      account.cards.published.includes(:rich_text_description).find_each(&:reindex)
      Comment.where(account: account).includes(:rich_text_body, :card).find_each(&:reindex)
    end

    def reconcile_storage
      account.boards.find_each(&:reconcile_storage)
      account.reconcile_storage
    end

    def fail_with(error)
      Rails.error.report(error, severity: :error) unless expected_failure?(error)

      erase_account
      update_columns(status: :failed, failure_reason: failure_reason_for(error), account_id: nil, updated_at: Time.current)

      Current.without_account { ImportMailer.failed(self).deliver_later }
    end

    def expected_failure?(error)
      error.is_a?(InvalidFileError) || error.is_a?(Account::DataTransfer::RecordSet::IntegrityError)
    end

    def failure_reason_for(error)
      expected_failure?(error) ? error.message : GENERIC_FAILURE_REASON
    end

    # Removes the account and everything that was written for it, including stored files and
    # people's identities that only existed because of this import.
    def erase_account
      if account
        delete_stored_files
        delete_account_records
        delete_created_identities
      end
    end

    def delete_stored_files
      ActiveStorage::Blob.where(account_id: account.id).find_each do |blob|
        blob.service.delete(blob.key)
      rescue => error
        Rails.error.report(error, severity: :warning)
      end
    end

    def delete_account_records
      account_id = account.id

      Search::Record.for(account_id).where(account_id: account_id).destroy_all
      Storage::Total.where(owner_type: "Account", owner_id: account_id).or(Storage::Total.where(owner_type: "Board", owner_id: Board.where(account_id: account_id).select(:id))).delete_all
      Filter.reflect_on_all_associations(:has_and_belongs_to_many).each do |association|
        Filter.reflect_on_association(association.join_table).klass.where(filter_id: Filter.where(account_id: account_id).select(:id)).delete_all
      end

      tenanted_tables.each do |table|
        Class.new(ApplicationRecord) { self.table_name = table }.where(account_id: account_id).delete_all
      end

      Account.where(id: account_id).delete_all
    end

    def tenanted_tables
      connection = ApplicationRecord.connection

      connection.tables.select do |table|
        table != self.class.table_name && !table.start_with?("search_records") && connection.column_exists?(table, :account_id)
      end
    end

    def delete_created_identities
      created_identity_ids = record_sets.grep(Account::DataTransfer::UserRecordSet).flat_map(&:created_identity_ids)
      Identity.where(id: created_identity_ids).where.missing(:users).find_each(&:destroy)
    end
end
EOF

cd /app; mkdir -p test/models/account; cat > test/models/account/import_test.rb <<'EOF'
require "test_helper"

class Account::ImportTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    @source = accounts("37s")
    @exporter = users(:jason)
    @identity = @exporter.identity
  end

  test "export and import round-trip preserves account data" do
    card = cards(:logo)
    card.image.attach(io: file_fixture("moon.jpg").open, filename: "moon.jpg", content_type: "image/jpeg")
    blob = ActiveStorage::Blob.create_and_upload!(io: file_fixture("avatar.png").open, filename: "avatar.png", content_type: "image/png")
    card.update!(description: "See <action-text-attachment sgid=\"#{blob.attachable_sgid}\"></action-text-attachment> and #{mention_html(users(:david))}")

    digest = account_digest(@source)
    path = export_account(@source)
    @source.incinerate

    import = import_file(path)

    assert import.completed?, import.failure_reason
    account = import.account
    assert_equal digest, account_digest(account)

    imported_card = account.cards.find_by!(number: card.number)
    assert_equal File.binread(file_fixture("moon.jpg")), imported_card.image.download
    embed = imported_card.description.body.attachables.grep(ActiveStorage::Blob).first
    assert_equal File.binread(file_fixture("avatar.png")), embed.download
    assert_includes imported_card.description.body.attachables, User.find(users(:david).id)

    assert account.users.find_by(identity: @identity).owner?
    assert_equal 1, account.users.where(role: :system).count
    assert_equal "Import Test" == account.name, false
  ensure
    FileUtils.rm_f(path) if path
  end

  test "importing into an instance that still has the data fails and leaves nothing behind" do
    path = export_account(@source)

    accounts_before = Account.count
    blobs_before = ActiveStorage::Blob.count
    users_before = User.count

    import = import_file(path)

    assert import.failed?
    assert_match "already exists", import.failure_reason
    assert_nil import.account
    assert_equal accounts_before, Account.count
    assert_equal users_before, User.count
    assert_equal blobs_before, ActiveStorage::Blob.count
  ensure
    FileUtils.rm_f(path) if path
  end

  test "a file that isn't an export fails with a reason" do
    tempfile = Tempfile.new([ "bogus", ".zip" ])
    tempfile.binmode
    writer = ZipFile::Writer.new(tempfile)
    writer.add_file "hello.txt", "Hello"
    writer.close

    import = import_file(tempfile.path)

    assert import.failed?
    assert_match "isn't a Fizzy account export", import.failure_reason
  end

  test "a file that isn't a zip fails with a reason" do
    tempfile = Tempfile.new([ "bogus", ".zip" ])
    tempfile.write("not a zip at all")
    tempfile.flush

    import = import_file(tempfile.path)

    assert import.failed?
    assert_match "valid ZIP", import.failure_reason
  end

  test "records pointing at other accounts are rejected" do
    path = export_account(@source)
    other_card = Card.where.not(account: @source).first || skip("no other account card")

    tampered = rewrite_zip(path) do |name, content|
      if name.start_with?("data/comments/")
        data = JSON.parse(content)
        data["card_id"] = other_card.id
        content = data.to_json
      end
      content
    end

    @source.incinerate
    import = import_file(tampered)

    assert import.failed?
    assert_match "isn't in this file", import.failure_reason
    assert_not Account.exists?(name: @source.name)
  ensure
    FileUtils.rm_f(path) if path
    FileUtils.rm_f(tampered) if tampered
  end

  private
    def export_account(account)
      export = Account::Export.create!(account: account, user: @exporter)
      export.build
      assert export.completed?

      Tempfile.create([ "export", ".zip" ]).path.tap do |path|
        File.binwrite(path, export.file.download)
      end
    end

    def import_file(path)
      Current.without_account do
        Account::Import.start(identity: @identity, file: Rack::Test::UploadedFile.new(path, "application/zip")).tap do |import|
          import.reload.process
          import.reload
        end
      end
    end

    def rewrite_zip(path)
      Tempfile.create([ "tampered", ".zip" ]).path.tap do |out|
        File.open(out, "wb") do |io|
          writer = ZipFile::Writer.new(io)
          File.open(path, "rb") do |source|
            ZipKit::FileReader.read_zip_structure(io: source).each do |entry|
              extractor = entry.extractor_from(source)
              content = +""
              content << extractor.extract(1.megabyte) until extractor.eof?
              writer.add_file entry.filename, yield(entry.filename, content)
            end
          end
          writer.close
        end
      end
    end

    def mention_html(user)
      "<action-text-attachment sgid=\"#{user.attachable_sgid}\" content-type=\"application/vnd.actiontext.mention\"></action-text-attachment>"
    end

    def account_digest(account)
      {
        name: account.name,
        users: account.users.order(:id).map { |u| [ u.id, u.name, u.role, u.active, u.identity&.email_address ] },
        boards: account.boards.order(:id).map { |b| [ b.id, b.name, b.all_access, b.creator_id ] },
        columns: account.columns.order(:id).pluck(:id, :name, :position, :board_id),
        cards: account.cards.order(:id).map { |c| [ c.id, c.number, c.title, c.status, c.board_id, c.column_id, c.creator_id, c.created_at.to_f, c.description.to_plain_text ] },
        comments: Comment.where(account: account).order(:id).map { |c| [ c.id, c.card_id, c.creator_id, c.body.to_plain_text ] },
        tags: account.tags.order(:id).pluck(:id, :title),
        taggings: Tagging.where(account: account).order(:id).pluck(:card_id, :tag_id),
        assignments: Assignment.where(account: account).order(:id).pluck(:card_id, :assignee_id),
        accesses: Access.where(account: account).where.not(user_id: nil).order(:id).pluck(:board_id, :user_id),

class Account::ExportTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "build creates a zip with the account data, readable cards, and files" do
    card = cards(:logo)
    card.image.attach(io: file_fixture("moon.jpg").open, filename: "moon.jpg", content_type: "image/jpeg")

    export = Account::Export.create!(account: accounts("37s"), user: users(:jason))

      export.build

    assert export.completed_at.present?

      manifest = JSON.parse(zip.read("manifest.json"))
      assert_equal Account::DataTransfer::Manifest::FORMAT, manifest["format"]

      assert zip.exists?("data/cards/#{card.id}.json")
      assert zip.exists?("data/comments/#{comments(:logo_agreement_jz).id}.json")
      assert zip.exists?("storage/#{card.image.blob.key}")
      assert_equal File.binread(file_fixture("moon.jpg")), zip.read("storage/#{card.image.blob.key}")

      readable = JSON.parse(zip.read("cards/#{card.number}.json"))
      assert_equal card.title, readable["title"]
      assert_includes readable["comments"].map { it.dig("body", "plain_text") }, "I agree."
      assert_equal "storage/#{card.image.blob.key}", readable.dig("image", "path")

      assert_not zip.exists?("data/users/#{users(:jason).id}.json") && JSON.parse(zip.read("data/users/#{users(:jason).id}.json")).key?("identity_id")
      assert_equal "jason@37signals.com", JSON.parse(zip.read("data/users/#{users(:jason).id}.json"))["email_address"]
    end
  end

  test "the export doesn't include its own file or other exports" do
    first = Account::Export.create!(account: accounts("37s"), user: users(:jason))
    first.build
    second = Account::Export.create!(account: accounts("37s"), user: users(:jason))
    second.build

    with_zip(second) do |zip|
      assert_not zip.exists?("storage/#{first.file.blob.key}")
      assert_empty zip.glob("data/exports/*")
    end
  end

  test "only the person who asked for it can download it, for a day" do
    export = Account::Export.create!(account: accounts("37s"), user: users(:jason))
    export.build

    assert export.accessible_to?(users(:jason))
    assert_not export.accessible_to?(users(:kevin))
    assert export.file.blob.accessible_to?(users(:jason))
    assert_not export.file.blob.accessible_to?(users(:kevin))

    travel 25.hours do
      assert export.expired?
      assert_not export.accessible_to?(users(:jason))
    end
  end

  test "cleanup removes expired exports" do
    export = Account::Export.create!(account: accounts("37s"), user: users(:jason))
    export.build

    Export.cleanup
    assert Export.exists?(export.id)

    travel 25.hours do
      Export.cleanup
      assert_not Export.exists?(export.id)
    end
  end

  test "a failed build is marked as failed" do
    export = Account::Export.create!(account: accounts("37s"), user: users(:jason))
    Account::DataTransfer::Manifest.any_instance.stubs(:each_record_set).raises(RuntimeError, "boom")

    assert_raises(RuntimeError) { export.build }
    assert export.reload.failed?
  end

  private
    def with_zip(export)
      ZipFile.read_from(export.file.blob) { |zip| yield zip }
    end
end
